evidence: Read query_database.py:266-361 at head. Guarded by try/except Exception: get_conversation (285-294), the scan _first_unanswered_tool_use (298-307), and the truncate call (322-345). Unguarded: agent.conversation_store (283), len(conversation.messages) (310, after the scan already iterated it), getattr(store, 'truncate_messages', None) (311, which only absorbs AttributeError, so a property raising another exception would propagate, contrary to the docstring's 'method lookup ... guarded'), user.id (323, inside the try, so guarded), and bool(removed_any) (346, unguarded). The rejection line (truncate_messages -> bool, no None) is covered: conversation_store.py declares the bool return, so a falsy value is logged, but it does not address a raising __bool__ or property. A concrete counterexample is a custom store whose truncate_messages property raises RuntimeError. That needs a non-shipped store implementation, so I could not show a shipped caller or documented state producing it. The docstring wording is slightly over-broad but I could not settle FAIL.

query_database.py:243-263 _first_unanswered_tool_use iterates range(start, len(messages)) and only returns an index in that range or None, so cut >= start. _trim_unanswered_tool_use (298, 323) passes that cut to truncate_messages, which keeps messages[:cut], so every message at an index below start survives. start is the baseline count read in _conversation_baseline (208-224) after the per-conversation turn lock is held, so earlier finished calls' messages sit below start. Absolute-claim probe: a store returning fewer messages than the baseline makes range(start, len) empty, so no cut (None). The result is the same if the baseline went stale because of an out-of-lock append, since appends only add indices above start. The claim holds for the code as written.

query_database.py: both _trim_unanswered_tool_use call sites (630-632 inside the inner `except Exception` handler, 635-637 after the inner try) sit inside the outer `try` opened at line 619, whose first handler is `except asyncio.CancelledError` at 638. In _trim_unanswered_tool_use (285-294) the get_conversation await is guarded only by `except Exception`, which does not catch CancelledError (a BaseException), so a cancel there propagates out of the helper to the caller's outer try. For a cancel raised at 630, the handler's own `raise` at 633 is never reached, and the CancelledError still propagates to the 638 handler. Absolute-input trace: a cancel while awaiting store.get_conversation at line 285 goes to 638 and rolls back to baseline_messages. The rejection line about truncate_messages returning None concerns a different subject and is not relied on.

Docstring (tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:4-13) claims a stopped call removes an unanswered tool_use or logs why not. Traced src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py. Absolute-claim input tried: the silent returns the hint names. (1) conversation is None (line 295-296): the conversation no longer exists (e.g. evicted), so no tool_use remains to reject; nothing to remove. (2) cut is None (308-309): _first_unanswered_tool_use found no unanswered tool_use, so nothing to remove. (3) queued_id None (lines 184-186, 629/634): conversation_id None means the agent mints a private id no later call can name (docstring 174-176), so no later request is affected; server.py always passes an id. In every case where an unanswered tool_use exists and the store is reachable, the outcome is removal (warning at 356) or an ERROR log: get_conversation raising (287), scan failure (300), no truncate_messages (313), ConversationOwnerMismatchError (325), other exception (337), falsy return (347; the rejection line about None returns is confirmed: truncate_messages is declared -> bool and a falsy return logs ERROR). Cancelled calls use _rollback_conversation (364+), which logs at ERROR on every failure branch. Claim about the Anthropic API rejecting the unanswered tool_use is consistent with the function docstring at 271-274. The silent returns do not contradict the claim because they only occur when there is nothing to remove.

criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text} objects and carries criterion 1 (same text as the claim); it was used, and the other criteria were read as limits. Code: query_database.py:638-649 catches asyncio.CancelledError (before the Exception handlers) and, when baseline_user and queued_id are set, calls _rollback_conversation(agent, queued_id, baseline_user.id, baseline_messages) and re-raises. The baseline length is read under the turn lock before the agent run (_conversation_baseline, :208-224). _rollback_conversation (:364-447) calls the synchronous BoundedConversationStore.truncate_messages (conversation_store.py:98-143), which does `del conversation.messages[length:]`. So the history is back to its pre-call length. The next call then sees no dangling tool_use. The test test_cancel_between_tool_use_and_tool_result_restores_history (tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:219-236) uses the real Agent, a BoundedConversationStore and a stub Anthropic client. It seeds one tool round, blocks run_sql, cancels once the assistant tool_use is saved with no result (asserts last role is assistant, :229), asserts CancelledError and history == before (:233), then _assert_next_call_succeeds (:209-216). That helper requires the markdown to start with 'Done.' and that every tool_use in the recorded request payload is directly followed by a tool_result with the same id (:182-197). Trigger split (the code condition `baseline_user is not None and queued_id is not None` plus the store guards in _rollback_conversation): (a) queued_id None (conversation_id None) -> outside the trigger, since the claim is about conversation C, a named id, and a None id means a private agent-minted id that no later call can name. (b) store lacks truncate_messages -> outside the trigger, since the claim specifies BoundedConversationStore, which has it. (c) truncate raises ConversationOwnerMismatchError -> outside the trigger, because the shipped _StaticUserResolver always returns the same user; it is also a runtime fault that logs ERROR and does not displace the cancellation. (d) truncate raises ValueError -> outside the trigger, because the length comes from len() so it is never negative; same fail-closed logging. (e) conversation evicted or unknown (truncate returns False) -> outside the trigger, since there is nothing left to restore and C then has no stale messages. (f) baseline read raising -> outside the trigger, because it happens before the agent saved anything and surfaces a sanitized RuntimeError.

query_database.py:243-263 (_first_unanswered_tool_use) collects ids from the assistant message, then walks messages[index+1:] collecting tool_call_id from consecutive role=='tool' messages, breaking at the first non-tool message; unanswered if ids not subset of answered. anthropic/llm.py:169-190 (_build_payload) groups consecutive role=='tool' messages directly into a single user message of tool_result blocks keyed by tool_call_id. This matches the claim: a tool_use is answered only by tool messages in the run directly after the assistant message. Absolute-claim trace: an assistant tool_use followed by an intervening user/assistant message then a tool message. The checker breaks at the intervening message, so it is unanswered, matching the API rule. Minor edge: the builder drops tool messages with falsy tool_call_id (llm.py:174), while the checker treats a None id as answerable by a None tool message (query_database.py:238-239,260). This needs a tool_use block with no id, which the API would reject anyway, and no shipped producer is shown creating one, so it does not break the claim. The rejection line about truncate_messages return values is unrelated to this claim.

agent.py:701 adds the assistant tool_use message before the tool loop; agent.py:861 awaits self.tool_registry.execute(tool_call, context) with no local try/except, so a raising replacement propagates before conversation.add_message(tool_response_message) at :1048 (no tool message saved). Agent.send_message (agent.py:174-227) catches Exception and yields an 'Error Processing Message' status card with status 'error'. _format.py:596,715 recognises that card title with status 'error' as the agent error, and query_database.py:702-708 then raises AgentRunError(_SQL_EXECUTION_ERROR_PREFIX + answer), where the prefix is 'SQL execution error: ' (query_database.py:93). The test (test_query_database_tool_history.py:236-253) matches this path. The later trim of the unanswered tool_use is the separate behaviour the test goes on to assert.

On the error path, query_database.py:607 calls _conversation_baseline, which does one store.get_conversation (line 221). Then agent.send_message makes exactly one get_conversation on the non-starter path (agent.py:431; the only other call, agent.py:301, is starter-UI only). The except at query_database.py:623-627 then calls _trim_unanswered_tool_use, whose get_conversation (line 285) is the third read. BoundedConversationStore.get_conversation is only defined (conversation_store.py:68) and nothing internal calls it, so the override counts no extra reads. The test arms the store after seeding (test file line 357), so reads counts from the call start, and `reads >= 3` raises at the trim's read, matching the comment at test lines 331-332.

Grep of truncate_messages across head src/ shows the only call sites are in src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py: line 321 inside _trim_unanswered_tool_use (defined line 266, called at lines 625 and 630) and line 395 inside _rollback_conversation (defined line 359, called at line 641 in the run path). The other hits are comments, log strings, or the definition at conversation_store.py:98. So there are exactly two production callers in tools/query_database.py, the rollback (cancellation handler) and the trim of an unanswered tool_use, as the docstring says. I did not read the context around line 641 to confirm it sits in the cancellation handler; _rollback_conversation's own docstring says it is called from a cancelled task. The rejection line about a None return concerns a different property and does not affect this claim.
